title: Kythera Cloud - Redwood partner discovery
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Kythera Cloud partnerships/infra. Discussed potential reseller/managed offering, compatibility with Kythera's GPU fleet and private VPC options, integration points for co-selling and joint benchmarks. Security posture and onboarding steps noted; agreed to follow up with partner deck, timing for pilot and shared benchmark plan.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Ravi Singh (Redwood SE); Jordan Kim (Redwood Partnerships); Lena Ortiz (Kythera - Partnerships); Evan Choi (Kythera - Head Infra); Grace Lin (Kythera - Solutions Architect); Omar Nadeem (Kythera - BD)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick partner intro, explored integration approaches (reseller vs hosted runs), compatibility questions around drivers/quantization, security checklist review, agreed next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on partner ops, with me is Ravi our SE and Jordan from partnerships, just to kick off—could folks quick intro on the kythera side?
[00:12] Lena: yeah hi I'm lena, head of partnerships at Kythera, we run a global GPU cloud focused on enterprise inference and managed models, Evan and Grace are infra and solutions respectively.
[00:20] Evan: hey all, happy to be here.
[00:22] Grace: hi everyone.
[00:25] Ravi: great, thanks. Wanted to surface we usually start with a short overview of how we think about partner models, and then deep dive on infra compat and a pilot plan if that makes sense.
[00:35] Lena: that sounds good — we're exploring both reseller and manage — excuse me — managed hosting options where we either resell Redwood hosted API or run Redwood private for customers on Kythera infra.
[00:46] Maya: perfect, good signal. Quick high level, Redwood provides hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments (VPC / on-prem). For partners we do both a reseller model and a private deployment partner — some partners host our private control plane and we ship the runtime, others prefer co-managed.
[01:00] Omar: question — what does the private deployment look like from a network perspective? we need to understand VPC peering, egress limits, and how keys are managed.
[01:09] Ravi: yeah, so our private option is a customer control plane, we can support VPC peering or private link, and keystone — sorry I mean KMS integrations. We support cloud KMS and external HSMs for keys. There's an audit log stream too.
[01:22] Evan: how intrusive is the runtime? we run a custom driver stack for some of our pascal and ampere nodes, and we use an internal orchestration layer.
[01:30] Ravi: the runtime is a user-space service that talks to the GPU via the standard drivers. For the most part we map to NVIDIA drivers and libnvidia, and we've got experimental support for a few AMD stacks; we do kernel selection at startup, and we can vendor a container with the right libs. We do prefer consistent driver versions for the large models to avoid memory corruption.
[01:48] Grace: and quantization profiles — do you require any special libcalls or kernel mods? we run a lot of int8 workloads.
[01:55] Ravi: good q. Our quantization-friendly execution path is mostly in user-space and doesn't require kernel modifications, but there are some perf-sensitive ops where a newer driver matters. And for int8 we expose recommended profiles and we've seen big perf wins with certain driver/blas combos.
[02:10] Lena: okay, from a business POV — how do you typically split revenue for reseller model? and is there co-selling enablement?
[02:18] Maya: we have a few templates — typically a percent rev share for reseller plus either credits for dedicated capacity or a pricing tier when customers are onboarded. We'll share the partner deck and partner MSA; co-sell motion is supported via lead registration and joint marketing funds for strategic accounts.
[02:35] Evan: on benchmarks — would you be open to running Redwood runtime on a small kythera cluster so we can joint publish performance numbers?
[02:42] Ravi: absolutely, that's our preferred path. We usually run a 2-week bench: one for baseline on our standard models (13B and 70B variants) with typical sequence lengths and a second for stress tests (burst, batching). We'll need a workload spec from you — batch sizes, p50 latency SLOs, and token distribution.
[02:59] Grace: we can share that; most enterprise customers target ~150 ms p50 for conversational workloads and higher for batch transforms. We also want cost/kg per token estimates from the bench.
[03:12] Maya: noted. We'll put together a short infra checklist and supported GPUs matrix — that will list recommended instance types, driver versions, and expected throughput.
[03:21] Lena: security is big for us — SOC2, iso, and data residency questions. do you have a standard security pack?
[03:28] Maya: yes — we have SOC2 Type II, ISO mapping, audit logs, SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC, and KMS integrations. We'll share our security whitepaper and SOC2 attestation. For private deployments we can offer additional audit hooks.
[03:41] Evan: any restrictions on bringing your own model weights? some customers want to host private licensed models.
[03:46] Ravi: bring your own weights is supported in private deployments — you'll want to confirm licensing and a secure storage path; we integrate with cloud object stores and customer KMS. There is a small onboarding checklist to validate model format and tokenizer mappings.
[04:00] (brief cross talk)
[04:05] Jordan: to align expectations: typical pilot looks like 4-6 weeks from kickoff to initial results — 2 weeks infra setup + 2 weeks bench + 1-2 weeks integration and reporting.
[04:17] Lena: that timeline works for Kythera. do you require an NDA before we share more infra details?
[04:22] Maya: a basic partner NDA is typical — we can share a mutual NDA and then the MSA.
[04:28] Evan: driver versions — we have mixed fleets with cuda 12 and older 11.x nodes; will that be a blocker?
[04:34] Ravi: not necessarily. We can run on different nodes but for production we recommend standardizing on a supported driver family; we'll include guidance in the matrix. There's also fallback options to smaller model variants if memory footprints are limited.
[04:48] Grace: on orchestration, we run Nomad in some datacenters and k8s in others; do you have a recommended deploy model?
[04:56] Ravi: we ship the runtime as container images and have deploy recipes for k8s and nomad. For bare-metal we provide a systemd unit and container runtime instructions. We do need to coordinate on network policies and mount points for kv cache if you use prefix caching.
[05:12] Lena: what about monitoring hooks — can we tie into kythera's telemetry stack?
[05:16] Maya: yes, we expose metrics via Prometheus endpoints and also have tracing hooks for requests. Redwood Console can forward logs and traces to a partner endpoint with proper auth.
[05:26] Omar: what's the expected unit economics for reselling the hosted API? is there an uplift?
[05:31] Maya: typically reseller uplift ranges depending on volume — we'll include sample pricing tiers in the deck. For Dedicated deployments we can do committed capacity pricing which is more predictable.
[05:41] Evan: curious about compatibility with third-party model formats like GGML or some of the community quantized formats, we get asked about that a lot.
[05:49] Ravi: we have support for a few community formats, but for best perf we recommend model conversion to our optimized graph; we can help with conversion as part of the pilot. Some community quant formats require custom kernels which can be brittle.
[06:05] Grace: what about telemetry and PII — can we filter logs before they leave kythera?
[06:10] Maya: yes, for private deployments logs can be routed to customer-managed sinks and we can enable PII redaction rules. Hosted API has configurable retention and scrub options.
[06:20] Lena: ok next, sales enablement — we'd want a pitch deck, technical integration guide, and a one-pager on commercial terms.
[06:27] Jordan: will prepare partner one-pager; Maya will attach the deck and high-level pricing. Ravi will attach infra checklist.
[06:33] Evan: for the benchmark, which models do you propose we run?
[06:36] Ravi: suggest 13B and 70B open variants (we can discuss exact model families); run common seq lengths 32/128/512 for chat and longer for transforms. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 plus tokens/sec for throughput.
[06:50] Grace: ok we will produce workload spec and a list of representative customers to mimic.
[06:56] Maya: great. Any blockers on legal — do you need a partner MSA before pilot?
[06:59] Lena: will check with legal but partner NDA first.
[07:03] (short pause)
[07:08] Omar: quick ops question — how do upgrades and rollouts happen on private deployments?
[07:12] Ravi: we support canary rollouts, A/B routing, and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if runtime upgrades fail. We also maintain a model catalog with verified performance profiles so customers can pin versions.
[07:26] Evan: if we spin up a pilot can you bring a small Redwood engineer onsite or remote to help?
[07:31] Maya: yes, SE support during pilot is standard; we typically allocate 2-3 SE days for onboarding and benching.
[07:38] Lena: timeframe — let's aim to sign NDA this week and schedule tech deep-dive next week.
[07:44] Maya: sounds good — we'll send the NDA and partner deck.
[07:47] (wrap)
[07:50] Maya: recap — Maya to send partner deck + NDA, Ravi to send infra checklist and supported GPU matrix, Lena to intro Sales lead, Grace to send workload spec. Schedule SE deep-dive for week of 2026-05-31.
[07:59] Lena: thanks all.
[08:01] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (KV cache -> KV cash; Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as Redwood Dedicate); some proper nouns may be off. Links shared: partner deck (link), security whitepaper (link), infra checklist (link - to be sent).
